findings.summary: ok=True on a satisfiable formula, both engines: deleting a reason clause leaves its literal in the root assignment but removes it from the RAT candidates, so a clause falsified at the root passes as vacuously RAT. (1)(-1 2), `d -1 2 0, -2 0, 0`

Both engines accept, and count as RUP, a clause not RUP or RAT on the clauses present, using a literal whose reason was deleted; docs say clauses present. Same root cause; implied by the input, so it does not by itself refute anything
Engines disagree on failed_clause when the failing step repeats a literal: Python removes repeats, native keeps them
ignored_deletions also counts deletions of clauses not present, including input tautologies CNF.add dropped, while report() calls them all unit deletions

not_checked: resolvents_checked is compared between engines only; the oracle has no opinion on the count
reason strings are compared between engines only
real solver proofs (cadical, kissat): every proof here is generated
drat-trim itself: it is not on PATH, so its behaviour is taken from the oracle's operational flavour, which over-approximates its reason test
the specified and length-one flavours: dratify documents operational
formulas above 10 variables, and long proofs: these are tiny by design
